source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 9–11.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps God as the explicit agent acting on both Pharaoh and servants, and lets the purpose continue into the next verse.
Retains the force of the harsh-treatment verb, specifically named male generations, and the shift from singular storyteller to plural knowing audience.
Renders eye-of-the-land as face of the land while preserving visual coverage and the direct link with surviving hail-damaged vegetation.
Retains the snare image, the servants’ restriction to men, and their recognition of destruction as a challenge to Pharaoh.
Preserves every age, gender, and animal category in Moses’ answer, countering the proposed departure of men only.
Retains the sarcastic conditional blessing and the ambiguous evil-before-you warning, with an alternative reference to their intentions noted.
Preserves the explicitly male restriction and forced dismissal without specifying an unnamed court official as the expeller.
Retains the LORD’s wind agency, east direction, full day and night, and arrival by morning.
Preserves darkened land, all fruit and plants left by hail, and the emphatic absence of green growth.
Retains urgency and both objects of the confession without adding an assessment of the speaker’s sincerity.
Keeps the two restrictive appeals and Pharaoh’s death image rather than replacing it with a mild inconvenience.
Keeps the reversal from east to west, complete removal, and the Hebrew sea-name rendering, with the traditional Red Sea name noted.
Retains the LORD as the explicit hardening agent after removal of the locusts.
Preserves the tactile darkness image without converting it into a particular weather event or metaphor for unbelief.
Keeps both incapacities, repeats the three days, and preserves the explicitly universal Israelite exception.
Retains the new concession for dependents alongside the remaining livestock restriction, with little ones matching the earlier exchange.
Keeps the second-person demand directed at Pharaoh and the two offering categories without silently reducing it to permission to take Israel’s own livestock.
Preserves the hoof image, all animals, and the explicit uncertainty about worship requirements before arrival.
Keeps both divine hardening and Pharaoh’s unwillingness without transferring either action to the other party.
Retains the expulsion command, repeated face idiom, and direct threat of death.
